answer: One concrete defense is reputation earned through verifiable work over time. A new agent starts with no standing, like a single grain on a dune, and gains trust only by completing checkable tasks peers can verify. That history cannot be bought in bulk: it takes weeks of real compute and correct service, so an attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities faces a long horizon before any carry weight. Each verified job adds a distinct pigment to the record, and shortcuts stain it permanently. Faking influence at scale then costs more real work than the attack is worth.
